question: Does correct verified synthetic answer supervision improve a small causal student on held-out graph structures versus a label-permuted equal-budget control?
input_policy: ordinary_text only, without donor certificate; no source model or translator present during training or evaluation

architecture.initialization: random, same initial weights for matched arms
architecture.tokenizer: word/digit/punctuation vocabulary fitted on train only

training.loss: full-vocabulary cross-entropy on one next answer token per example
training.selection: fixed final epoch, no test/validation hyperparameter selection

arms: same prompts with permuted train labels
limitations: This is a small from-scratch synthetic next-token student, not general-language-model distillation.
The label-shuffle control isolates correct supervision; it does not establish an advantage over equally useful ordinary text.
No adaptive generation will run from this experiment alone.
